status: Design guesses for optical studies, labelled as such: what the Open Moon's seas carry. Earth's waters are the reference and engineered life a design variable. Each value has a best guess and a range.
reading_rule: chlorophyll_mg_m3 is chlorophyll a in the sunlit surface layer, standing for the phytoplankton and the particles that vary with them; dissolved_organic_440_per_m is the absorption of coloured dissolved organic matter at 440 nm; fines_g_m3 is suspended regolith by dry mass, with the soil that sets its colour. The light cycle scales chlorophyll between dawn and dusk.

open_sea.description: Nutrient-poor open water, far from rivers and shores
open_sea.basis: Earth's subtropical gyres hold 0.02-0.1 mg/m3 of chlorophyll and the open ocean's median is about 0.2; open-ocean coloured organic matter absorbs 0.01-0.04 per metre at 443 nm (Nelson and Siegel 2013). Wind-borne regolith over open water stays a small, unknown range.

productive_coast.description: A coast fed by rivers and upwelling, with waves stirring regolith from the shore
productive_coast.basis: Earth's shelf seas and upwelling coasts hold 1-10 mg/m3 of chlorophyll; European coastal waters carry organic absorption of 0.03-1 per metre and 0.1-60 g/m3 of suspended matter (Babin et al. 2003). Fines settle six times slower at lunar gravity, so the same stirring keeps more aloft.

river_mouth.description: Where a river from the rain-fed lakes meets the sea
river_mouth.basis: Earth's estuaries and river plumes reach 5-20 mg/m3 of chlorophyll, organic absorption above 1 per metre and tens of grams per cubic metre of sediment.

soils.12001: mare fines, Apollo 12 soil from Oceanus Procellarum
soils.10084: darker high-titanium mare fines, Apollo 11 soil from Mare Tranquillitatis
soils.62231: bright highland fines, Apollo 16 soil from the Descartes highlands

light_cycle.basis: Through the 15-day day phytoplankton grow as far as nutrients allow; through the 15-day night they respire and are grazed. Losses of 0.05 a day for 15 days leave about half the biomass at dawn, so a sea is greenest at dusk.
